APPLICATION 02 / REACH

Underwater Tunnel Inspection ROVs

A long tunnel needs a complete mission plan.

Inspection of flooded water tunnels depends on navigation, tether control and recovery as much as the vehicle’s rated range.

Home / Applications / Long-distance underwater tunnel inspection

Who this is for

Hydropower operators, water-conveyance asset owners and specialist inspection contractors.

Project inputs

  • Tunnel route, cross-sections and bends
  • Water depth, flow and operating restrictions
  • Entry point, deployment area and isolation arrangements
  • Required defect coverage, location reference and recovery plan
Build a project brief

The short answer

Long-distance underwater tunnel inspection uses a specialised ROV to travel kilometres through flooded headrace and water-conveyance tunnels. The AD-400 is designed for this task, with a 5 km official operating range. Success depends on route geometry, tether management, position referencing and a recovery plan.

01

Map the route before selecting the system

Provide the tunnel length, section, gradient, bends, constrictions and known obstructions. A straight test route cannot establish performance through an arbitrary tunnel geometry.

02

Engineer power, communications and tether handling

The AD-400 uses an external tethered system. Review tether storage, deployment, bend contact, drag and retrieval. Verify how the complete package maintains power and communication over the intended route.

03

Tie findings to a position reference

Agree how inspection distance and location will be referenced, what uncertainty is acceptable and which instruments support it. Request actual data samples rather than relying on a positioning feature name.

04

Agree an abnormal-event recovery plan

Document the response to power or communication loss, snagging, sediment obstruction and unexpected flow. Define the retrieval equipment, access arrangements and site responsibilities.

05

Verify range against the actual mission

The official AD-400 page lists a maximum operation distance of 5 km; the supplied brochure lists 5.5 km. Neither figure is a universal guarantee. Confirm the supplied version, conditions and project acceptance test.

BEFORE YOU SPECIFY

Frequently asked questions.

Does this apply to every penstock?

No. Pressure conduits differ in geometry, flow and access. Treat each penstock as a separate engineering review rather than assuming tunnel capability transfers.

Can inspection proceed without shutdown?

Operational access depends on flow, isolation, permits and the owner’s procedures. A shutdown-free mission should only be promised after site-specific review.
